Operator
Good day, welcome to the Imperial Oil Q2 2025 earnings call. Today's conference is being recorded. At this time, I'd like to turn the conference over to Peter Shaw, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.
Peter Shaw
VP of Investor Relations, Imperial Oil
Good morning, everyone, welcome to our Q2 earnings conference call. I am joined this morning by Imperial Senior Management team, including John Whelan, Chairman, President, and CEO. Dan Lyons, Senior Vice President, Finance and Administration. Cheryl Gomez-Smith, Senior Vice President of the Upstream, and Scott Maloney, Vice President of the Downstream. Today's comments include reference to non-GAAP financial measures. The definitions and reconciliations of these measures can be found in attachment six of our most recent press release and are available on our website with the link to this conference call. Today's comments may contain forward-looking information. Any forward-looking information is not a guarantee of future performance, actual future performance, and operating results can vary materially depending on the number of factors and assumptions.
Forward-looking information and the risk factors and assumptions are described in further detail on our Q2 earnings release that we issued this morning, as well as our most recent Form 10-K. All these documents are available on SEDAR+, EDGAR, and our website. I'd ask you to reference those. John is going to start with some opening comments and then hand it over to Dan, who's going to provide a financial update, and then John will provide an operations update. Once that's done, we will follow with Q&A session. With that, I will turn it over to John for his opening remarks.
John Whelan
Chairman, President, and CEO, Imperial Oil
Thank you, Peter. Good morning, everybody, and welcome to our Q2 Earnings Call. I hope everyone is doing well. I am really pleased to kick off my first earnings call with strong results for the Q2. We generated cash flow from operations of nearly CAD 1.5 billion and ended the quarter with approximately CAD 2.4 billion of cash on hand. We achieved these results while successfully completing significant planned turnaround activity across our integrated portfolio. At the macro level, our Upstream price realizations continued to benefit from improved egress in Western Canada. While in the Downstream, margins were supported by higher crack spreads since the last quarter. Our resilient business model and strong financial position have allowed us to remain focused on delivering safe, reliable operations while executing on our business plans and strategy despite significant market volatility.
I also want to highlight some major project milestones we achieved in the quarter. At Kearl, we completed work that doubles the turnaround interval at one of our two trains. The next turnaround of the K2 train is now scheduled for 2029. At Cold Lake, we finished construction of the new SAGD redevelopment project at Leming and initiated steaming in the final days of the quarter, setting us up for first production late this year. At Strathcona, construction of the renewable diesel facility was completed, and I'm very pleased to share that first production of renewable diesel began in July.
When I think broadly about the outlook for future investment, I'm very encouraged by the constructive dialogue and level of engagement with the federal government and the work that is now ongoing to potentially support industry and major projects in Canada. It's still early, but initial conversations have been encouraging. Finally, our philosophy of returning surplus cash in a timely manner is unchanged. As such, I'm pleased to announce that we've chosen to accelerate share repurchases through our NCIB once again and plan to complete the program by year-end. On that note, I'll turn over to Dan to discuss our financial results in more detail.
Dan Lyons
SVP of Finance and Administration, Imperial Oil
Thanks, John. Starting with financial results for Q2, we reported net income of CAD 949 million, down CAD 184 million from Q2 2024, primarily driven by lower Upstream realizations, partly offset by higher production volumes. When comparing sequentially, Q2 net income is down CAD 339 million from Q1 2025, primarily driven by lower Upstream realizations and Downstream margin capture. Now shifting our attention to each business line and looking sequentially. Upstream earnings of CAD 664 million are down CAD 67 million from Q1, primarily due to lower realizations, partially offset by higher volumes. Downstream earnings of CAD 322 million are down CAD 262 million from Q1, mainly reflecting lower margin capture.
Our Chemical business generated earnings of CAD 21 million, down CAD 10 million from Q1. Moving on to cash flow. In Q2, we generated CAD 1,465,000,000 in cash flows from operating activities. Excluding favorable work from capital tax of CAD 52 million, cash flows from operating activities for Q2 were CAD 1,413,000,000, down CAD 95 million from Q2 2024, in line with earnings. As John mentioned, we ended the quarter in a strong position with about CAD 2.4 billion of cash on hand. Shifting to CapEx, capital expenditures totaled CAD 473 million in Q2, CAD 11 million higher than Q2 2024, primarily due to project timing.
In the Upstream, Q2 spending of CAD 353 million focused on sustaining capital at Kearl, Syncrude, and Cold Lake. In the Downstream, Q2 spending related primarily to our renewable diesel project at Strathcona. Now in terms of shareholder distributions, we paid CAD 367 million of dividends in Q2 2025. On 23 June, we announced the renewal of our normal course issuer bid, which allows us to purchase up to 5% of our outstanding common shares over the next 12 months. We started purchasing ratably in July, and as John noted, we plan to accelerate our purchases and complete the program prior to year-end, in line with our long-standing practice of returning surplus cash to shareholders. Lastly, this morning, we announced the Q3 dividend of CAD 0.72 per share, in line with our Q2 dividend.
Now I'll turn it back to John to discuss our operational performance.
John Whelan
Chairman, President, and CEO, Imperial Oil
Thanks, Dan. I want to take the next few minutes to share the key highlights from our operating results. Upstream production for the quarter averaged 427,000 oil equivalent barrels per day, up 9,000bbl per day versus Q1, up 23,000bbl per day versus Q2 of 2024. This marks the highest Q2 production in over 30 years. I am extremely pleased to see our asset teams deliver such strong results in the quarter that included turnaround activity at both Kearl and Cold Lake. For the H1 of the year, we achieved the highest ever production from our heavy oil assets and are well positioned for a strong H2 of the year. Moving to Kearl.
Kearl set a record, a Q2 production record averaging 275,000bbl per day gross, up 19,000bbl per day versus the Q1. We beat our previous Q2 record by 20,000bbl per day gross. This year's Kearl plan turnaround on the K2 train was a major success. The turnaround was completed safely and successfully in under 19 days. The team also completed work to enable a doubling of the turnaround interval. As we outlined at our Investor Day, turnaround optimization is one of the key components of our plan to increase production to 300,000bbl per day. Turning to costs, Kearl's unit cash costs in the quarter were $18.86 US per barrel.
We realized a decrease of nearly $2 US per barrel compared to Q1, including the expense of our planned turnaround. When compared to Q2 last year, we achieved a decrease of over $3 US per barrel. The Q2's performance contributed to our year-to-date unit cash costs of $19.70 US per barrel, nearly $2 US per barrel lower versus the H1 of 2024. With the turnaround behind us and our outlook for higher volumes in the H2 of the year, we expect to make further progress on unit cash cost reductions. Moving to Cold Lake. Cold Lake production averaged 145,000bbl per day, including 23,000bbl per day from Grand Rapids.
This is down 9,000bbl per day versus Q1 2025, primarily driven by planned turnaround at Mahkeses, which was completed safely and well ahead of schedule. Another highlight is reaching a key milestone at our Leming SAGD redevelopment project. The project started steam injection in June, with first oil expected late this year and ramping up in 2026. The Leming SAGD project is an excellent example of how we are maximizing value from our existing assets. This is a niche opportunity for us to develop additional resource at the original Cold Lake pilot location with 9,000bbl per day at peak production.
I also want to take a moment to provide a brief update on the EBRT pilot project at our Aspen lease, which utilizes transformative new solvent technology that's designed to unlock low cost, low emissions volume growth from our significant high quality, undeveloped in situ opportunities. We completed several key construction milestones this quarter and remain on track for an early 2027 startup. Next, I want to quickly cover Syncrude. Imperial's share of Syncrude production for the quarter averaged 77,000bbl per day, which was up 4,000bbl per day versus the Q1 and up 11,000bbl per day versus the Q2 of 2024. Syncrude continued to utilize the interconnect pipeline to import bitumen and gas oil to ensure high upgrader utilization. This enabled an additional 8,000bbl per day, our share of Syncrude Sweet Premium production.
In early September, I'll note that Syncrude will begin its 50-day coker turnaround with a forecasted annual impact of 6,000bbl per day to Imperial share. Now moving to the Downstream. We refined an average of 376,000bbl per day, reflecting a utilization of 87%. This compares to 387,000bbl per day a year ago, and 397,000bbl per day in Q1. Lower throughput reflects higher unplanned downtime and the impacts from planned turnarounds at Strathcona and Nanticoke compared to our Q1 2025. During the quarter, we completed construction and commissioning of the renewable diesel facility located at the Strathcona refinery. I'm very excited to announce the successful startup and first production in July. As we've said before, we now plan to optimize production around supplier capabilities.
This project, at its peak, generated close to 600 jobs and was completed safely while achieving industry-leading cost and schedule performance. The project provides a new lower emissions offering to Canada's transportation sector and aligns with our long-term strategy of advancing responsible energy solutions while delivering strong returns. This project combines many of our competitive advantages, including integration, proprietary technology, scale, advantaged logistics, and proximity to feedstocks and markets. When you couple these advantages with the growing demand for renewable diesel in Canada, driven by layered provincial and federal regulations and increasing demand from customers to meet their own emissions reduction goals, we are confident in robust margin uplift as we ramp up in line with third-party hydrogen supplies.
I would just like to thank our planning, project, and operations teams that have worked extremely hard to get this project across the finish line. I'd also like to thank the governments of Alberta and British Columbia, as well as Strathcona County for all of their support. Moving to petroleum product sales. Petroleum product sales in the quarter were 480,000bbl per day, which is up 25,000bbl per day versus Q1 2025, and up 10,000bbl per day versus Q2 2024, enabled by the Trans Mountain pipeline expansion. Turning to Chemicals. Earnings in Q2 were CAD 21 million, down CAD 10 million versus Q1. Compared to Q2 2024, earnings were down CAD 44 million, driven primarily by soft polyethylene margins and the aromatics reporting shift to our Downstream segment, which occurred in Q3 2024.
Now, while we're at the bottom of the cycle, we see bottom of cycle conditions, and those have persisted. The business continues to contribute positively given strong operational performance and the integration with the Sarnia refinery. To wrap up, I'm very pleased with the quarter. We generated about CAD 1.5 billion of cash from operating activities while successfully executing on significant planned maintenance. We set new Q2 production record in our Upstream. Since my return to Imperial Oil, it's been wonderful to reconnect with the organization and the initiatives across the business that will drive continued momentum and growth, specifically the disciplined development and deployment of technology to support the execution of our strategy, maximizing value from our existing assets, and supporting our growth investment opportunities.
This quarter was a great example of the team finding ways to win. Winning starts with taking full advantage of our unique competitive advantages others do not have. During the quarter, it was fantastic to achieve a significant milestone in our Downstream with the completion of the renewable diesel facility and first production just a couple of weeks ago. At Cold Lake, we completed, as I mentioned, the Leming SAGD project that begun steaming the reservoir. I'm looking forward to first oil late this year. It was great to meet many of you at our Investor Day in mid-April. I've really enjoyed connecting with more of you in recent meetings and conferences. I'm very excited about the path forward for Imperial, and I'm looking forward to further engagement with you in the coming months.
As I look ahead to Q2 of the year, we've got momentum. It's significant turnaround work behind us, we'll continue to focus on safe and reliable operating performance while progressing our growth initiatives. As we announced this morning, we plan on accelerating share repurchases under the normal course issuer bid. I'm pleased to say that our strategy of responsibly increasing cash flow and delivering unmatched shareholder returns remains alive and well. To wrap up, I'm extremely proud of what our team has delivered, I want to recognize and thank them. As always, I'd like to thank you for your continued interest and support. With that, now we'll move to the QA session. I'll pass it back to Peter.
Peter Shaw
VP of Investor Relations, Imperial Oil
Thank you, John. As always, we'd appreciate it if you could limit yourself to one question plus a follow-up so that we can get to as many questions as possible. With that, operator, could you please open up the lines for questions?
Operator
Thank you. If you would like to signal with questions, please press star one on your touch tone telephone. If you're joining us today using a speaker phone, please make sure your mute function is turned off to allow your signal to reach our equipment. Again, that is star one if you would like to signal with questions. Our first question comes from Manav Gupta with UBS.
Manav Gupta
Executive Director, UBS
Good morning. My first question is, it relates to is the decision to accelerate the NCIB. Okay, can you help us understand why this decision was taken? In terms of cash balances, how confident are you that you can complete this entire NCIB without levering up, but before year-end? Thank you.
John Whelan
Chairman, President, and CEO, Imperial Oil
Thank you, Manav. Good morning. Thank you for your question. We are very comfortable and confident. When we look at where commodity prices are, we look at how our business is performing, we look at the cash that we have on hand and our projections around free cash flow as we look forward. We are very comfortable in accelerating the NCIB and comfortable that we will do that without leveraging our balance sheet. We can do that with free cash flow. This is very consistent for us. As you know, we've got strong appetite for shareholder returns. We've got a track record of doing this. We've returned CAD 20 billion to shareholders since 2020. CAD 15 billion of that has been share buybacks.
This is very consistent with us, and we're extremely confident we're gonna do this from free cash flow.
Manav Gupta
Executive Director, UBS
Perfect. My follow-up is a little bit of a tricky question, but I'm going to ask it anyways. When we look at year-to-date relative outperformance, you have strongly outperformed your peers. You're an absolute and a relative winner. What that does is sometimes people just want to come after you because they believe this cannot continue. I'm just trying to understand from, in your opinion, why does the management feel the setup is still very strong, for our investment case for Imperial, where it could continue to work on an absolute and a relative basis as we move along, despite the very strong year-to-date outperformance?
John Whelan
Chairman, President, and CEO, Imperial Oil
I think it comes back to our strategy to win and our competitive advantages. Our strategy is all about responsibly increasing cash flow and delivering unmatched industry-leading shareholder returns. We think we have a very strong basis to do that. We believe we've demonstrated that in our past performance. Continuing to focus on maximizing the value of our existing assets. We've talked about the improvements we're making at Kearl and Cold Lake. Investing selectively in growth opportunities at those existing assets, Kearl, Cold Lake transformation, Strathcona renewable diesel, and then progressing future strategic growth.
If you think about our EBRT pilot and the growth opportunities that we have in our portfolio, we are very bullish about what that technology is gonna deliver in the future and the asset base we have in terms of our heavy oil in situ portfolio. I think our strategy to win is strong. We've continued to focus on that. I believe we have competitive advantages that when matched up against those assets that we have. Take our unique competitive advantages around scale and integration, technology, execution, and the best team in the business. When we take those competitive advantages against the advantage assets, that leads to value creation in the future, and that's what comes back to us continuing to deliver unmatched industry-leading shareholder returns.
We are very confident that the performance we've had is on the basis of that strategy and the teams and the technologies and our competitive advantages, and we're gonna continue to deliver that going forward.
Manav Gupta
Executive Director, UBS
Thank you for the detailed response. Just for the record, we completely agree with you. We believe the setup is very strong for your stock to continue to work. Thank you.
John Whelan
Chairman, President, and CEO, Imperial Oil
Thank you, Manav. Thanks for the questions and your confidence in us.
Operator
The next question comes from Dennis Fong with CIBC World Markets.
Dennis Fong
Equity Research Analyst, CIBC World Markets
Hi, good morning. Thank you for taking my questions, and congratulations on a strong operational quarter despite planned maintenance. My first question goes a little bit into the technology side. You've been operating an autonomous fleet now for a little while, and I was hoping to dive into some of the insights that you might have gained from running and deploying this technology. Can you outline some of maybe the surprising benefits you've observed thus far with AHS deployment on your existing asset base?
John Whelan
Chairman, President, and CEO, Imperial Oil
Morning, Dennis, and thanks. Thank you for your question. When I think about the autonomous haul system, which has been a huge success and very proud of what the team has done there. It's part of a broader technology approach that we have, and I talked about our competitive advantages, and technology is the first one on the list that I mentioned. For us, technology is the core to what we do. I mean, we're more than an oil and gas company. We're more than an energy company. We're really a technology company that's managing molecules. This autonomous haul system, for as successful as that's been, it's part of a broader approach around technology.
It's in our digital journey that we're on, the automation journey that we're on. We talked about EBRT, the technologies that we've applied. It's part of a broader ecosystem and a way of working and part of our DNA. Now, specifically, though, on the autonomous haul system, because it has been an amazing success, and it's phenomenal when you go there and see these 80+ trucks all working autonomously. I would say, I don't know that there's been. We had high ambitions for it. We anticipated it would reduce our unit cash cost by about CAD 1 a barrel. It has done that. Now. I don't know that we were surprised by anything. I think it's worked well.
I think we see actually even further optimization of that because now we're gonna look at ways to further optimize the fleet. We think we're still tuning the vehicles in an autonomous way. Then we have other autonomous opportunities around robotic fueling of the trucks. Robotic inspection of the vehicles, and we're considering other equipment in our fleet that we could automate. I think if you think about the upside is we stepped into it with heavy oil trucks and there's more to go.
Dennis Fong
Equity Research Analyst, CIBC World Markets
Great. Thanks, John. I really appreciate that color. My second question stays on Kearl and focuses a little bit on unlocking the full potential of the equipment that you're using at site. I wanted to kinda dive a little bit into hydrotransport lines and what you guys are doing there to improve, again, runtime and maybe space between turnarounds. If you wouldn't mind also touching on what also drives confidence in moving towards a four-year interval rather than the two-year interval.
John Whelan
Chairman, President, and CEO, Imperial Oil
Yeah. No, thanks for that question, Dennis. If you think about where we're trying to get to with Kearl and moving it now, we we're at CAD 280, and now we're gonna look at getting it to CAD 300 and further lowering our unit cost to CAD 18 a barrel. Now, there's three legs to that stool that we're focused on right now. There were others that got us there in the past, but the ones we're focused on now is enhancing the recovery, improving the productivity and the reliability gains, leveraging technology again, and then turnaround efficiency. Those are the three areas.
Enhancing recovery is enhancing the recovery in the mine and enhancing the recovery in the plant to get more bitumen out of the oil sands, basically. Improving the productivity is looking at every piece of kit that we have, our trucks, our shovels, our dozers, our hydrotransport lines, and improving the productivity and reliability of those. We talked about the turnaround efficiency. Specifically on the hydrotransport lines, and some of the things we've done with that is we've interconnected our crushers to allow for flexibility. We have enhanced the metallurgy of the lines to improve the life and the wear that we're seeing on the lines, and then we've upsized them as well, so we can get more product through.
That allows us, when we do have downtime on one part of our equipment, we can run more through the hydrotransport lines. It's a question of configuration and interconnection of our equipment. It's the metallurgy we're using in the lines, and then it's the size of the lines. Working on all of those three things, that's specifically what we've worked around on hydrotransport lines. In terms of our confidence, you may have heard me talk about before. Our goal is to be the most responsible operator, not just a responsible operator, but the most responsible operator. That involves safety and environment, it involves reliability and our cost structure, all of those things.
When we think about what we're doing on the turnarounds and the extension that we've had over time, reducing the duration, extending the intervals, that's one of the best examples I can point out to about being the most responsible operator, 'cause we do that in a way that will not in any way compromise safety, integrity, or reliability. We're getting those benefits through plowing our learnings back into our turnarounds, continuous improvement and learnings, not only from our operations, but from our major shareholders' operations. It's applying technology. It's applying new equipment and managing the wear of our assets and building in redundancy. Executing with higher efficiency and using things like abseilers versus scaffolding and so on. We're doing all that in no way compromising safety, integrity of our assets.
Dennis Fong
Equity Research Analyst, CIBC World Markets
Great. Thanks, John. Really appreciate that detailed answer. I'll turn it back. Thanks.
John Whelan
Chairman, President, and CEO, Imperial Oil
Thanks, Dennis.
Operator
We'll take a question from Greg Pardy with RBC Capital Markets.
Greg Pardy
Managing Director and Head of Global Energy Research, RBC Capital Markets
Yeah, thanks. Good morning. John, I was hoping maybe to dig into some of your opening remarks. I'm gonna try and shoehorn three questions in here with Peter not noticing. Just with renewable diesel, I know you were talking about just optimization in terms of suppliers. Does that mean then that you will be likely producing more renewable diesel in the summer and fall versus the winter months? Then does that kinda tie into fuel specs? Just curious as to how you'd be running that new unit.
John Whelan
Chairman, President, and CEO, Imperial Oil
Yeah. Thanks, Greg. I'll start then I might ask Scott to chime in as well. If I step back from it wasn't getting to seasonal aspects really. First, let me say extremely pleased with starting off this project and obviously the team is going through optimizing production right now. The way we've looked at this project, there's three kinda key parts to this. It's one is, at its core is the manufacturing facility that we built at the Strathcona refinery. That's complete. It's up and it's running. We're very pleased at the ramp-up and how that's gone. It's, I would say, exceeding expectations, if anything.
The other big component is the vegetable and agricultural oil feedstock that needs to come in to feed the project. Then the other part is the supply of hydrogen. That when we talked about that optimizing the inputs, it's around optimizing the feedstock that comes in and the supply of hydrogen to run the facility. I would tell you on the first one around the vegetable and agricultural oil stocks, all those arrangements are in place, and the supply is in place, and we're very comfortable with that.
On the hydrogen, we have sufficient grey hydrogen to start up and to operate the facility, but the availability of further hydrogen supplies and blue hydrogen will impact the speed and the ramp-up of the asset. What we were really referring to there is the ramp-up. The hydrogen supplies, the availability of hydrogen supplies, and how that comes into the market. That's kind of what we were referring to.
Greg Pardy
Managing Director and Head of Global Energy Research, RBC Capital Markets
Okay.
John Whelan
Chairman, President, and CEO, Imperial Oil
I'll just flip over to Scott, if you have anything further to add on that, Scott.
Scott Maloney
VP of Downstream, Imperial Oil
Yeah, yeah. Thanks, John. Just one additional point for you, Greg. Your comment around when we'd like to operate the facility. We'll absolutely be operating this facility year-round. In fact, we'll especially like to be operating it in the winter months as we take advantage of the proprietary catalyst technology that we have as part of this project that enables a lower pour, lower cloud product that can be run in operational year-round. We'll be blending this product into diesel products that we sell into the market year-round, and that's one of the advantages we have as part of this project.
Greg Pardy
Managing Director and Head of Global Energy Research, RBC Capital Markets
Okay. Terrific. Two other, maybe just more or less footnotes. John, did you say there was a little more unplanned downtime just in refining? Just curious if there's any color around that. Then are you still producing 4,000bbl or 5,000bbl a day of solvent at your new solvent-aided project at Cold Lake? That's it for me. Thanks.
John Whelan
Chairman, President, and CEO, Imperial Oil
Yeah, I think you're right. We did say that we had a little higher unplanned and planned downtime in the Downstream in Q2. The planned, the shutdown work went extremely well, basically ahead of schedule and lower on cost. We're very pleased with that. We did have a little uptick in unplanned downtime in the quarter. Nothing significant, nothing that concerns me. It's actually behind us now, so really nothing specific there. The question on the solvent. Sorry, was that? Can you repeat that one?
Greg Pardy
Managing Director and Head of Global Energy Research, RBC Capital Markets
Yeah. No. Are you still producing more or less five to— is the circa— I think you mentioned circa 23,000bbl coming out of the Grand Rapids. Is 4,000bbl to 5,000bbl of that still solvent basically you're injecting?
John Whelan
Chairman, President, and CEO, Imperial Oil
No, that 23,000bbl is bitumen. That's on a bitumen basis. We're producing 23,000bbl a day of bitumen from that project.
Greg Pardy
Managing Director and Head of Global Energy Research, RBC Capital Markets
Okay. Understood. Thanks very much.
John Whelan
Chairman, President, and CEO, Imperial Oil
Thanks, Greg.
Operator
We'll take a question from Menno Hulshof with TD Securities.
Menno Hulshof
Managing Director of Equity Research, TD Securities
Thanks. Good morning, everyone. I just have one question on the CapEx side of things. You were quite a bit lower in the quarter than we were modeling. What drove that? Given that you're trending below last year in the quarterly run rate implied in your full year guidance, what should we expect the cadence of spending to look like in Q3 and Q4? Finally, is it possible that we see Imperial test the lower end of the guidance range of CAD 1.9 to 2.1 billion?
John Whelan
Chairman, President, and CEO, Imperial Oil
Thanks, Menno. I'll make a few comments, and maybe I'll ask Dan to kinda chime in as well. What we're really seeing here is just timing. It's really a timing effect on the capital. At this stage, there is no change to our, to our guidance in the CAD 1.9 to 2.1 billion, as you stated. We do expect spend to be modestly higher rate in 2025 and 2026, as you know as well, but it's just for what you're seeing in 2025, it's just the timing, milestone payments and things like that, and the time which they hit. Right now, we're still consistent with our guidance. Anything else?
Dan Lyons
SVP of Finance and Administration, Imperial Oil
Yeah. No, that's exactly right. It really is just timing. We're comfortable with our guidance. We'll have a little bit more spend over the back half of the year.
Menno Hulshof
Managing Director of Equity Research, TD Securities
Terrific. Thank you. I just thought of another one. Just on the EBRT side of things, just to dig a little deeper, what is the status of the three horizontal well pairs that you recently drilled? Are they already in the early stages of activation? If not, what is the timeline that you're targeting?
John Whelan
Chairman, President, and CEO, Imperial Oil
Yeah. No, they're not yet, Menno. Like I say, we've drilled them. That's part of the work we've been doing at site to get the site ready. We've got the wells in place, but we still have the facilities, the surface facilities to build to allow us to be injecting the solvent. That's the startup of that is planned for early 2027, and that's when we'll start to inject solvent and a little bit of steam into those wells will be at that time.
Menno Hulshof
Managing Director of Equity Research, TD Securities
Terrific. Thank you.
John Whelan
Chairman, President, and CEO, Imperial Oil
Thanks, Menno.
Operator
Our next question will come from Patrick O'Rourke with ATB Capital Markets.
Patrick O'Rourke
Managing Director of Institutional Equity Research, ATB Capital Markets
Hey, guys. Good morning, thank you for taking my question. The first question, you talked about refined product sales going up to 480,000bbl a day here being enabled by the Trans Mountain expansion. If you could maybe unpack that a little bit more. I'd be curious to know from a margin perspective, what the impact here would be on the margins at the refinery level from that.
John Whelan
Chairman, President, and CEO, Imperial Oil
Yeah. I'll start. Thank you for your question, Patrick, and I'll kick off and I'll again probably ask Scott to chime in a little bit. If you look at that, what we were referring to there, we're always working to enhance our Downstream market position and our ability to efficiently supply customers. We did pick up some additional refined product supply flexibility with Trans Mountain, and we did take advantage of that in Q2. Overall, our sales, though, are dictated by demand, and we've seen steady demand in Canada year-over-year on all the products basically that we are supplying. That we're seeing that steady demand. We picked up a little extra space on Trans Mountain, which we took advantage of in the quarter.
That was a mix of local sales and profitable export opportunities. It's all about efficient logistics and having the flexibility and the market expertise to take advantage of the demand when it's there, and that's exactly what we did in the quarter. I'll just ask Scott if he wants to chime in a little more.
Scott Maloney
VP of Downstream, Imperial Oil
Sure. Yeah. I'd just add to that our primary route to market is the manufactured products that our refineries move through our proprietary midstream logistics systems to supply primarily domestic demand across the Canadian marketplace. The comment there was just reflecting the fact that as we see opportunities with some spot space available on that Trans Mountain expansion pipeline, we always consider utilizing logistics that are out there to move product to different markets to take advantage of demand and uplift potential. That's really what that comment referred to.
Patrick O'Rourke
Managing Director of Institutional Equity Research, ATB Capital Markets
Back to the second part, is there a margin enhancement there, or is it just purely volumetric?
Scott Maloney
VP of Downstream, Imperial Oil
Yeah. All of our movements are meant to generate margins. All that's a positive return for us. As I mentioned before, we're primarily placing our sales into the domestic market, and that's where we see the higher uplift.
Patrick O'Rourke
Managing Director of Institutional Equity Research, ATB Capital Markets
Okay. You touched on Kearl a little bit here. I think that the results there were a bit ahead of where we had it modeled in the quarter.
